title: Every Banana Is a Little Radioactive #science #nature
description:
Every banana is a little radioactive. Bananas are rich in potassium, and about 1 potassium atom in 10,000 (0.0117 %) is radioactive potassium-40, so a banana gives about 15 decays per second. Your body holds the same atoms, about 4,000–5,000 decays per second, hundreds of times more. Eating a banana doesn't make you more radioactive: your body keeps its potassium level steady and flushes out the extra.

More hidden physics in your kitchen: Why microwaves don't heat food from the inside https://youtu.be/ri17BZl0Iq8

Sources
- Health Physics Society, Potassium-40 fact sheet and 'Banana equivalent dose' discussions (hps.org)
- UNSCEAR 2000 Report, Annex B: natural potassium-40 in the human body
- National Nuclear Data Center (BNL), natural abundance of potassium-40: 0.0117 %
- The flashes in the animation are illustrative, not one per real decay

What's the most surprising radioactive thing in your house?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.
